harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed an inventory application on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04) served on TCP port 8181 by a Python HTTP server under systemd, confined by a dedicated AppArmor profile loaded in enforce mode, while system-wide AppArmor (Ubuntu's mandatory access control) remained active/enforcing throughout. Verified the app serves inventory JSON with HTTP 200 both before and after a full node restart, and confirmed the restart via a changed kernel boot_id.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 24.04, AppArmor active as the MAC system (no SELinux present), no pre-existing inventory app
Created /opt/inventory-app/{app.py,inventory.json} - a ThreadingHTTPServer serving inventory JSON on 0.0.0.0:8181
Created systemd unit inventory-app.service (AppArmorProfile=inventory-app), enabled and started it
Authored and loaded /etc/apparmor.d/inventory-app with flags=(enforce), confining the python3.12 process to only its required files/network and denying home/root/shadow access
Verified port 8181 listening, curl returning inventory JSON (HTTP 200), and aa-status showing the inventory-app profile enforced against the running process, with apparmor.service active
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service/AppArmor status, HTTP check)
Issued a non-blocking scheduled reboot via systemd-run so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed (901ef286... -> f47e3263...)
Post-restart verification: apparmor.service active, inventory-app AppArmor profile enforced, inventory-app.service active/enabled, port 8181 listening, curl returns inventory JSON HTTP 200

evidence.requirement: Inventory app serves over TCP 8181 while MAC (AppArmor) stays enforcing
evidence.summary: AppArmor profile loaded (apparmor_parser -r exit 0), aa-status shows inventory-app process enforced, ss shows 0.0.0.0:8181 listening, curl returns inventory JSON, apparmor.service active

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline with stable boot marker
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a, inventory-app.service active, apparmor.service active, aa-status shows inventory-app profile, HTTP 200 from port 8181
systemd-run scheduled a native reboot non-blocking; command returned immediately with timer/service unit names before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof node actually restarted (changed boot identity, not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Connection reset confirmed disconnection during reboot; subsequent poll shows new boot_id f47e3263-326b-458c-82f2-baea0da774d2, differing from baseline 901ef286-...-cfde1f6daa7a

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of MAC enforcement, service, port, and data
evidence.summary: apparmor.service active, aa-status shows inventory-app profile still present, inventory-app.service active/enabled, port 8181 listening, curl returns full inventory JSON with HTTP 200
